cands.name: Taylor Cook

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Democratic candidate for Alabama House District 43 in 2026. Born in Hattiesburg, Mississippi, and raised in Geneva, Alabama. Has worked in auto shops, warehouses, retail management, a law firm and general aviation. Finishing a political science degree online. Has held no elected office.
cands.gaps: We found no record of Cook holding public office, so there are no official actions to report. We found no statements from him on data centers, development or growth limits, restrictions on investor or foreign land buyers, H-1B visas or immigration enforcement, police pay or public order, gun laws, or abortion. He says generally that he will protect Alabama's natural resources and protect renters and homeowners from corporate abuse, without specifics. His platform mentions campaign finance reform, but we found no pledge about refusing particular kinds of donations. His exact jobs, employers and dates of work are not listed, and we could not find when his family moved to Alabama.

cands.name: Arnold Mooney

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Republican member of the Alabama House of Representatives for District 43 since November 2014. Commercial real estate businessman with over 40 years in the field. Ran in the 2020 Republican U.S. Senate primary, finishing with about 1%. Was an at-large Alabama delegate to the 2016 Republican National Convention.

endorsements.text: 2014 House campaign endorsements listed by Ballotpedia included Manufacture Alabama, the Alabama Association of REALTORS, Gun Owners of America and Eagle Forum of Alabama president Eunie Smith. Ballotpedia found no endorsements for his 2026 race.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Arnold Mooney was born or raised, or when he came to Alabama. No page shows a specific bill he sponsored or an action he took in office, so we can't say what he did on data centers, homestead taxes, land buying, growth, policing or school funding. We found no documented stances from him on data centers or development, and no controversies. The campaign pages we read date from his 2020 U.S. Senate run, and his 2026 campaign statements were not available. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2020, 2022 or 2026.

second-amendment.evidence: Said he strongly believes in the Second Amendment and that it "is not up for debate or discussion" (campaign site from his 2020 U.S. Senate run).

pro-life.evidence: Said "Life is precious and begins at conception" and that he holds an unwavering belief in safeguarding the unborn's right to life (campaign site from his 2020 U.S. Senate run).

workers-first.evidence: Said he would "go to war" with anyone who sells out Alabama workers for cheap illegal labor, and that existing immigration laws are not being enforced (campaign site from his 2020 U.S. Senate run).

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Said parents should be able to choose the school that best meets their children's needs and that decisions should be placed in parents' hands (campaign site from his 2020 U.S. Senate run). The page does not mention teacher pay.
